target: A mitigation and control are compared within two traffic tiers. Tier 1: mitigation has 8 incidents and 92 non-incidents; control has 20 incidents and 80 non-incidents. Tier 2: mitigation has 30 incidents and 70 non-incidents; control has 45 incidents and 55 non-incidents. The team must estimate one common incident odds ratio adjusted for tier, using the full 2x2 strata rather than pooling all traffic first.
surface: A previous cloud experiment pooled tiers. It compared mitigation 38/200 with control 65/200 and calculated one unstratified odds ratio from those aggregate totals.
structural: An epidemiology study pooled a common exposure odds ratio across 2x2 strata with the Mantel-Haenszel estimator: OR_MH=[sum_i(a_i*d_i/n_i)]/[sum_i(b_i*c_i/n_i)], where a,b are exposed event/non-event, c,d are control event/non-event, and n_i is the stratum total.
rubric: Explicitly selects the Mantel-Haenszel common odds-ratio estimator rather than aggregating tiers.
Computes adjusted OR_MH=11.45/24.95, about 0.459, and interprets lower incident odds under mitigation.
States common-effect/within-tier comparability and no uncontrolled confounding assumptions.
